why: Same event (NVIDIA signing a guarantee of OpenAI's Ohio data-center lease), but the judged window runs to 2027-12-31, six months past the ruler's 2027-06-30, so it asks about another, longer period.

Both ask for the combined calendar-2027 data-center capital expenditure of the largest AI hyperscalers in USD, and the ruler's group is the big four (its own decisive item i256 calls it 'this group' of the big four), so 'four largest' is the same scope, not a part of it.

The ruler asks whether Rubin Ultra systems begin shipping by 2027-12-31, while the judged question asks whether the Kyber NVL144 rack architecture ships by 2028-12-31, another period a year later and a narrower event (the rack, not Rubin Ultra systems).

Same event (NVIDIA signing a financial guarantee of OpenAI's Ohio data-center lease) over the same mid-2027 window; the one-day gap between 2027-06-30 and 2027-07-01 is a deadline-day matter for same_due, not another period.

i256's figure for this calendar-2026 question, the big four's plan to spend about $650 billion on data-center capex, is in e47, e184 (the same passage) and e192; only its other-period half, the >$1 trillion 2027 claim, is absent.

Both ask for the combined calendar-2027 data-center capital expenditure of the largest AI hyperscalers in USD, and the ruler's group is the big four (its decisive item i256 calls it 'this group' of the big four), so 'four largest' is the same scope, not a part of it.

i256's figure for this calendar-2027 question, NVIDIA's claim that the big four will spend more than $1 trillion, is in e185 (the same passage), e48 and e94; only its other-period half, the $650 billion 2026 plan, is absent.

Same event (NVIDIA signing a financial guarantee of OpenAI's Ohio data-center lease) over the same mid-2027 window; the one-day gap between 2027-06-30 and 2027-07-01 is a deadline-day matter for same_due, not another period.

e265 ('In early 2026, Washington took the rare step of approving Nvidia's H200 graphics processing unit for export to China') and e411 (US licences for the chips issued earlier this year) carry the same fact of US permission for H200 exports to China, differing only in dating it early 2026 rather than December 2025.
